ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly high-intensity white background (approx. 65%) with high-density low-intensity black pixel clusters (approx. 35%) creating a high-contrast speckled distribution.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous dark pigmentation along the entire upper trailing edge and lower peduncle junction. High-density mottled clusters of irregular black spots distributed across the medial and distal white regions of both lobes, with larger contiguous dark blobs on the inner-left lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression with an acute interior angle of approximately 52 degrees relative to the primary lobe axes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency micro-serrations (2-4 pixel amplitude) along the length of the trailing edge, interspersed with larger, irregular notches on the distal posterior margins, particularly on the left lobe.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex curvature along the lateral boundaries, tapering towards sharp, slightly upturned posterior-lateral tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Global distribution of roughly circular dark pixel clusters (2-12 pixels in diameter) consistent with pigmentation spotting or barnacle attachment scarring, most dense in the medial sections of the lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A distinct, dark, unaligned horizontal linear disruption (rake mark) located on the right lobe near the median notch; several faint, short vertical linear markings on the lower-left ventral surface.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent horizontal linear scar on the medial-right lobe surface; multiple irregular chips and notches along the trailing edge margins indicative of physical trauma or environmental wear.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique high-frequency spotting density ('salt-and-pepper' pattern) that is nearly continuous towards the distal tips of both lobes.
